lane: Native-resolution lidar scarp channels: slope-aware scarplet template (Sare & Hilley JOSS 2018 doi:10.21105/joss.01066; AGU 2015 T31A-2838 slope-aware extension) + Steger (IEEE TPAMI 20(2):113-125, 1998) + Frangi (MICCAI 1998 LNCS 1496:130-137) on slope-detrended aggregate of 2 m descriptors; sigma 1-4 x 100 m cells (100-400 m) — native 2-20 m execution not measured (raw 1 m tiles unreachable here).
hypothesis: Young, sharp, antislope scarps that persist along strike at 300/500/900 m are the expert-added faults missing from the catalogue; allocating the dot budget across relief terciles by footprint share removes the range-front confinement that reversed LIDAR-01 on the basin floor (IR-74).
mechanism: rank01( (0.25*sharp + 0.25*persist + 0.20*polarity + 0.15*frangi_rank + 0.10*coh_rank + 0.05*steger_rank) * (0.5+0.5*sqrt(step_rank*ex_rank)) ); greedy emission, >=3 px separation, >2 px (200 m) from catalogue, K=37654, relief-tercile allocation by eligible-footprint share (truth-free).
named_nonfault_mimic: Fluvial terrace risers / irrigation canal banks (sharp, persistent, single-sided steps); suppressed only by antislope polarity + cross-slope veto — no pinned cultural-feature mask exists in this checkout.
